notes.title: Job words
notes.text: Many job titles end in a suffix: -가 for experts and creators (화가 painter, 작가 writer, 예술가 artist, 전문가 expert), -자 for people who do something (과학자 scientist, 기자 reporter), -원 for staff (공무원 civil servant, 회사원 office worker), -사 for licensed professions (변호사 lawyer, 의사 doctor, 요리사 cook).

scene.ko: 도윤 씨가 제이미를 회사에 초대했어요. 작은 게임 회사예요.
scene.en: Do-yoon invited Jamie to his company. It's a small game company.

scene.ko: 어서 오세요. 제 명함이에요. 저는 이 회사의 대표예요.
scene.en: Welcome. Here's my business card. I'm the head of this company.

scene.ko: 와, 대표님이세요? 직원이 몇 명이에요?
scene.en: Wow, you're the boss? How many employees do you have?

scene.ko: 사원은 열 명이에요. 여직원이 여섯 명이고요. 다들 직장 생활을 즐겁게 해요.
scene.en: Ten staff. Six of them are women. Everyone enjoys their work life.

scene.ko: 몇 시에 출근해요?
scene.en: What time do you start work?

scene.ko: 평일 아침 열 시에 출근하고, 저녁 일곱 시에 퇴근해요. 출근이 늦어서 좋아요.
scene.en: Weekdays we come in at ten and leave at seven. It's nice that we start late.
b: to be good, to be nice

scene.ko: 회사가 커지면서 업무가 많아졌어요. 퇴근도 늦어졌어요.
scene.en: As the company grew, the workload got bigger. We leave later now too.
b: to be many, to be a lot

scene.ko: 사무실이 정말 밝아졌네요! 근무하기 좋아 보여요.
scene.en: The office has gotten so bright! It looks like a nice place to work.
b: to be good, to be nice

scene.ko: 근무 시간은 길어졌는데 일은 더 재미있어졌어요. 하하.
scene.en: The hours got longer, but the work got more fun. Haha.

notes.title: 명함
notes.text: Business cards (명함) are given and received with both hands and a slight bow. Look at the card for a moment before putting it away — never stuff it in a back pocket. A company head is the 대표 (or 사장), and staff call them 대표님.

notes.title: Konglish tech words
notes.text: Tech vocabulary is mostly English in Korean clothes: 컴퓨터, 모니터, 프로그램, 파일, 메일 (email), 홈페이지 (website), 피시 (PC). A 피시방 is a gaming café, open late and very cheap.

notes.title: Interview Korean
notes.text: Interviews use very polite speech: 저는 … 경험이 있습니다 (I have experience in …), 열심히 하겠습니다 (I'll work hard), and 감사합니다 at the end. Interviewers often ask about your strengths (장점) and weaknesses (단점) — have an answer ready!

notes.title: 수고하셨습니다
notes.text: Korean offices run on set phrases. Leaving before others: 먼저 들어가 보겠습니다 (I'll head out first). Thanking people for their work: 수고하셨습니다. A newcomer says 잘 부탁드립니다 — "please treat me well." 시키다 also means "to order" food: 짜장면 시킬까요?

notes.title: 대기업 and start-ups
notes.text: Korea's economy is famous for its giant conglomerates (대기업, also called 재벌) like Samsung and Hyundai. Those jobs are prized, but many young Koreans now leave to start small companies — especially in games, where Korea is a world leader.
